  "required_fixes": [
    "C06-A02-RF01 [P2] Preserve uncertainty and partial effects during avatar replacement. crates/desktop-core/src/academy.rs:565 collapses lost PUT replies and HTTP failures into UploadFailed; authority/learner_domain.rs:968 returns Rejected for every failed/cancelled PUT, and :978 also treats a refused confirmation as rejection of the whole upload. However, Academy's pinned server/services/avatar.ts uses the stable avatars/{userId}.{ext} key: overwriting an existing avatar changes its publicly served bytes before confirmAvatar. A store can accept the bytes and lose its reply, or confirmation can fail after a successful overwrite. The desktop then reports 'Your photo is unchanged; try again' (use-avatar-upload.ts:90), with no readback. An independent in-memory execution of the actual synthetic store reproduced changed public bytes after a lost PUT response without confirmation; actual hostAction/useAvatarUpload code mapped the supplied native Rejected result to that unchanged claim and zero settings refreshes. Acceptance: distinguish pre-upload refusals/known rejection from uncertain PUT outcomes and effects already applied before failed confirmation. Report possible/partial changes truthfully, support appropriate readback even when the stored avatar URL has not changed, and do not automatically resend mutations. Add production-interface tests for an existing avatar overwritten before a lost PUT reply, cancellation/server failure after dispatch, and successful PUT followed by denied confirmation, including the composed learner message/readback.",
    "C06-A02-RF02 [P2] Restore bounded image preparation and validate decodable photos. apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/adapters.rs:337 limits the selected source file directly to Academy's 2 MiB upload cap; crates/desktop-core/src/avatar.rs:48-66 checks only leading bytes and AvatarJob uploads the original file unchanged. The pinned working-v1 baseline 74754c02 (src/ui/academy/profile_media.rs:187-239) accepts source photos up to 16 MiB, bounds decoding to 8192 pixels/128 MiB, applies orientation, and crops/re-encodes a 512-pixel square below the 2 MiB upload cap. Consequently ordinary 2-16 MiB photos that worked in v1 are rejected, while truncated JPEG/PNG/WebP headers can be uploaded and confirmed as broken avatars. Current tests explicitly accept such non-images; the Rust integration 'png' contains a signature followed by text. Acceptance: implement bounded native decoding/preparation with the retained source-photo capability, orientation and square output, keeping Academy's final upload cap and credential/destination restrictions. Test real decodable larger source photos, orientation/output dimensions, malformed files retaining valid magic bytes, and decoder dimension/allocation limits; invalid images must cause no upload."
  ],
  "blockers": [],
  "evidence_gaps": [],
  "optional_suggestions": [
    "crates/desktop-core/tests/academy_program/main.rs:230 still supplies obsolete runId/alertId/choice inputs to shift.answer and runId to shift.serve. Align this scheduling fixture with the actual shiftId/order/values and shiftId/order contracts. The native C06-N06 evidence already uses the correct shape, so this remains optional.",
    "Consider exposing a load-failed state from useLearnerImage. When the native loader returns null, Settings receives no src and silently shows initials, so AvatarUploadHero's image-error message cannot explain that an existing photo could not be read."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "All four supplied fingerprints, the 308-entry source inventory, 95 referenced artifacts and source-bound run/log/artifact hashes were independently verified; the passing C05 predecessor receipt and Academy bd8942141154e703f94c9525348c23127fa6a13d tree matched. Frozen inputs were checked again before writing this verdict.",
    "Prior timer and draft-ordering findings are resolved: independent in-memory React probes mounted the actual shared timer through the updated header bridge and observed exactly one expiry submission; three overlapping draft-save requests produced two serialized writes on bases 0/1 and retained confirmed version 2. Course reset and lesson feedback are restored. Print-open failure now has observed native-operation results and composed/native fixture evidence.",
    "Independently executed the existing synthetic academy_program binary (13/13 passing) and five avatar unit tests (5/5 passing), without rebuilding. Reviewed registered evidence for 174 desktop tests, 1350 hermetic shared tests, 38 core tests, 71 selected frontend tests, the current truth-graph gate and 21 guarded mutation probes. Those passing tests omit the avatar cases in the required fixes.",
    "Independent JavaScript probes used actual pinned functions/hooks with real React DOM/JSDOM and scripted boundaries. The avatar overwrite probe executed actual Python fixture handlers entirely in memory, without a server/socket or file writes. The native lost-PUT outcome classification was established by Rust source inspection, not a newly compiled adversarial Rust test.",
    "All 55 submitted C06/C01/C04/C05 native checks report pass on executable 6776e04ffa7e2a3ddfc11cda06bc8aa6e0777652c4277f4b6dcabd75e8476548. Relevant AX trees, driver code and request records were inspected; native interaction was not repeated. The fixture substitutes a staged avatar picker and recording printer; actual NSOpenPanel/print-sheet interaction and spoken VoiceOver output were not exercised. Dismissal after a print sheet opens is not reported as an exported file.",
    "Inspected credential confinement, learner-generation retirement, destination restrictions and hosted grading/award boundaries remain intact. The authority/security score is reduced for incorrect remote-outcome reporting in the new avatar workflow, not an observed credential or assessor-authority bypass.",
    "No application source was changed, no product endpoint was called and no real credential was accessed. Hosted qualification remains C25 and signed installed-package qualification remains C26; the previously recorded typed-input accessibility memory issue remains assigned to C24."
  ],
